title: 6 months progress
author: spixt
selftext:
I keep getting downvoted or get nasty comments by the anti AI folks so wanted to share this here.   I end up deleting a lot of the threads I create just because I don't want negativity in my attempts to garner attention for my game.   But whatever.

Here's my game, Giblings. It comes out in a bit over a week on Steam. I started the project last year in a slow and unproductive way of learning Godot and typing things out character by character.  Then around 6 months ago my wife got me the gift of a 12 month Claude Code subscription and **my god** did my life change after lol.    The progress here is actually 4months of work, not 6,  because in those first 2 months I barely touched it as I was always busy or tired, and I thought it was more important to focus on mastering Godot by writing out lines of code by hand.   

BOY WAS I WRONG, it is just a very archaic way of thinking. I have been a software engineer for 20 years and although I was sad that I have lost the challenge of solving coding problems and learning, I'm getting far more enjoyment **FEELING LIKE A GOD WHO CAN CREATE ANYTHING** with claude code.  I literally stopped playing games, stopped reading novels and stopped watching Netflix because I rather work on my game then any of that.   *I don't get tired anymore*.  4 months ago, I was always tired the moment I clock off work of my corporate job so I end up doing nothing productive after, but somehow with using coding agents my energy levels has increased 1000x and know I could do this 18 hours a day now as long as I had the financial freedom to do so.   
  
My regret now is not that AI has changed my profession forever, but that I wasted the first 2 months of that Claude Code subscription. Or that I didnt pay for one myself even earlier than that.  I could have been almost done with my 2nd game by now! XD 

Anyhoo, here's the Steam link if anyone was interested in checking it out. I just submitted a demo for review so that should land next week sometime. 

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5025950/Giblings/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5025950/Giblings/)

replies.author: spixt
replies.body:
\>Would you say there was a moment of being able "edit as fast as you can think?"

Only in the early days. Once the codebase passes the \~20,000 lines of code mark it slows.  My project is at around 100,000 lines of code and small tasks can take time now.  The test suites alone take about an hour to run, so what I would normally do is get a whole bunch of minor edits at once before running the full suite.  

For major tasks, I run the full suite of tests at every change. So it takes time.  

You don't want to do major edits without running the full suite.  I did that in early days too and the bugs that got introduced were bad, and could only be solved using git bisect which was painful and slow. 

\> I'd made a routine to easily get AI to push gameplay out directly to video, so I had it go through the archives and make me a montage of my own progress. Would love to see other people share the longer messy processes that isn't just "I set a millions agents to make a AAA game, make no mistakes".

Nice work.  Just note that you can just git checkout earlier commits and do the same in one go without having to create a video every day. But the tokenmaxxing lifestyle is about having fun not about being efficient, so ignore me if you prefer your way of creating the montage ;) 

Good luck on your game!  I think it'd be awesome you made it an online co-op game.

replies.author: johnesco

comments.author: Dankedest444
comments.body:
Why does your steam ai disclosure say it was hand authored?:  
“*The rest of the game's content, including the characters, animation, weapons, visual effects, sound and gameplay, is all hand-authored. Nothing is generated by AI during gameplay.”*

replies.author: spixt
replies.body: Because it was.  Sounds are all public domain that I found. Gameplay, weapons are all designed by me.  Characters were drawn by me then translated to code.   Steam does not require you to disclose the usage of coding agents, just the parts that are presentable to the end user.  They are very clear about that.

replies.author: HumbleWorkerAnt
replies.body:
> Characters were drawn by me then translated to code

what's 'translated to code'?

not having a dig btw, i like the project i'm just curious

replies.author: spixt
replies.body:
e.g. if you draw a circle with a dot in it to represent an eye, then pass that to your coding agent that examines the image, then converts that sketch into a big empty circle with a little filled black circle inside --  that is drawn by code.    
  
I used that technique for all characters, which is why the characters are all big circles essentially (but I hid that with big eyes, hair styles, feet etc).  That look works though for the cartoony vibe I was going for, and for when the characters are quite small on your screen.   Won't work if your game needs something bigger and more realistic looking, which most do.
